stem: Which finding is classically associated with chronic bronchitis rather than emphysema?

options.A: Alveolar-wall destruction with permanent enlargement of distal air spaces, the pathologic pattern associated with emphysema.
options.B: Abrupt pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea caused by air in the pleural space, a presentation consistent with pneumothorax.
options.C: Isolated exertional dyspnea without a chronic productive cough, which does not meet the classic chronic-bronchitis definition.
options.D: Persistent productive cough for at least 3 months per year for 2 consecutive years after other identifiable causes have been excluded.

rationale: The 2026 StatPearls edition defines chronic bronchitis in adults as a persistent productive cough without another identifiable underlying cause lasting at least 3 months per year for 2 consecutive years. D directly matches that classic definition. The other options describe emphysema, pneumothorax, or a symptom pattern that does not meet the chronic-bronchitis definition.
educational_objective: Recognize the classic adult clinical definition of chronic bronchitis: productive cough for at least 3 months annually in 2 consecutive years after excluding other causes.

source_original.stem: Which finding is classically associated with chronic bronchitis rather than emphysema?

options.A: Alveolar-wall destruction with permanent enlargement of distal air spaces, the pathologic pattern that defines emphysema.
options.B: Abrupt pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea caused by air in the pleural space, the typical presentation of pneumothorax.
options.C: Isolated exertional dyspnea without a chronic productive cough, which does not meet the classic chronic-bronchitis definition.
options.D: Persistent productive cough, classically present for at least 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years after other causes have been excluded.

source_original.rationale: Chronic bronchitis is classically defined by persistent productive cough for at least three months per year in two consecutive years, whereas emphysema is characterized by destruction/enlargement of distal air spaces.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect for chronic bronchitis; describes emphysema pathology.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; isolated exertional dyspnea without chronic productive cough does not meet the classic definition.
